products.name: Rev AI
products.note: Speech-to-text API; transcription; captioning; human + AI hybrid; data confidentiality

reading.body:
Rev's primary AI product is a speech-to-text API with hybrid human review, positioned for legal transcription where recordings must become courtroom-admissible documents.

The company has built its AI application around a constraint that most AI services ignore: legal admissibility. A transcription only becomes evidence if it can withstand cross-examination. This shapes every layer of Rev's product. The API handles the initial conversion from audio to text, but the platform routes outputs through human review before they become final. This hybrid approach is not a limitation of the AI but a feature of it, because the cost of error in legal settings is discontinuous. The company's framing as "turning digital evidence into verified, citable findings" reflects this. The concentration of its legal exposure data in Texas, where it holds an official partnership with the State Bar, suggests the company has built distribution through regulatory trust rather than API ubiquity.

Rev's model demonstrates that not all AI products are compute-first. The bottleneck here is neither chip capacity nor power availability. It is the human review step, which is part of the product architecture itself. This matters for AI ecosystem mapping because it shows compute abundance does not automatically flatten industries where liability, proof standards, or audit trails remain binding constraints. The data does not reveal Rev's infrastructure scale, power consumption, or data center strategy, so this page cannot assess whether Rev itself is constrained by power or compute density. It only shows how one company has positioned AI where institutional trust matters more than inference speed.

profile_text.body:
Rev is a for-profit startup founded in 2010 and headquartered in Austin, TX, USA. Its website describes the company as an "Investigative Intelligence & Legal Transcription Platform" built for investigations that hold up under court. Rev says its legal AI platform turns digital evidence into verified, citable findings, with every finding linking back to a citation with the exact timestamp and source file. The site lists features including multi-file evidence analysis, a document editor, image analysis, transcript editor and clipping, AI templates, and a mobile app.

Rev's tracked product is Rev AI, a speech-to-text API for transcription and captioning that offers human and AI hybrid options and data confidentiality. The company states that AI transcription is included with every subscription and returns a 96%+ accurate transcript in minutes, while human transcription is 99%+ guaranteed and completed in under 12 hours. Pricing starts at $0.25/min for AI transcriptions or captions, $1.99/min for human transcriptions or captions, and $6.49-15.99/min for global subtitles. Rev says its AI reduces hallucination risk by only pulling findings from uploaded files rather than searching the internet.

Rev has 126 law exposure entries in Texas and no recorded cases. It is associated with six MCP server entries: ai.knowall/reverie, ai.meltstudio/peer-review, ai.powerline/inbox-preview, ai.revelara/mcp, ai.revuo/revuo, and ai.truverif/panel-review.
